feedback.problem: The coefficient of ${x}^{7}$ in the expansion of ${(4+x)}^{9}$ is
feedback.worked_solution:
The binomial theorem states that for any positive integer $n,$ we have

 

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\frac{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\frac{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\frac{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+⋯+(\frac{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

In the case of ${(4+x)}^{9},$ we have $a=4,$ $b=x,$ and $n=9.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}(4+x)^{9}=(\frac{9}{0}){4}^{9}{x}^{0}+(\frac{9}{1}){4}^{9-1}{x}^{1}+(\frac{9}{2}){4}^{9-2}{x}^{2}+⋯+(\frac{9}{9}){4}^{9-9}{x}^{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the ${x}^{7}$ term must be

$$
(\frac{9}{7}){4}^{9-7}{x}^{7}.
$$

Evaluating the coefficient, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{9}{7}){4}^{9-7} & =36\cdot {4}^{2} \\  & =36\cdot 16 \\  & =576.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coefficient of ${x}^{7}$ is $576.$
